subject: psychology
title: Forensic Psychology: Custodial Sentencing & Rehabilitation
welcome_lead: Prison, anger management, restorative justice — what actually reduces reoffending?
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology custodial sentencing recidivism, anger management, restorative justice.
final_note: Punishment alone is not deterrent enough.

concepts.def: Loss of identity in prison environment, sometimes increasing aggression.
CBT-based programme: cognitive prep, skill acquisition, application.
Mediated meeting between offender and victim.
Operant conditioning programme using token economies.

walkthroughs.body_html: Prison aims at deterrence, incapacitation, retribution and rehabilitation. UK recidivism within one year is around 48% (Ministry of Justice 2013). Psychological effects include stress, depression and institutionalisation; suicide rates in UK prisons are roughly nine times higher than community.

Novaco's anger management has three stages: cognitive preparation (identifying triggers), skill acquisition (relaxation, assertiveness) and application practice (role-play). Ireland (2004) found 92% of treated UK young offenders showed improvement vs none in controls.

Restorative justice brings victim and offender together. Sherman & Strang (2007) reviewed 36 studies: lower reoffending and higher victim satisfaction. Best results for violent crime; weaker for theft. UK Restorative Justice Council reports 85% victim satisfaction.
